jess: Quick loop 0449 I'm putting together a small docs PR that clarifies rollback behavior for Dedicated when an autoscale rollout fails, plus a tiny Node SDK snippet and a pointer to the rollback CLI. Can someone glance for accuracy?

marco: Yep please include exact CLI command that's supported by redwoodctl v1.9.0 so ops can copy-paste. Also add a short note about metrics lag causing overscale then rollback.

jess: Draft copy for the "rollback" subsection:
"If a scalepolicy rollout results in instability (increased error rate or sustained latency), the orchestrator will automatically attempt a rollback to the previous policy. Rollbacks may take up to two cooldown windows to complete as running replicas are drained gracefully. During rollback, traffic may be routed to fallback model variants or a lower-priority pool. To trigger a manual rollback: use the CLI or SDK command below."

nina: Suggest adding a one-line caution: "Manual rollbacks can cause transient token-cost spikes if traffic is rebalanced across more expensive model variants."

jess: Node.js SDK snippet (short):
```javascript
const { DedicatedClient } = require('@redwood/inference');
const c = new DedicatedClient();
// trigger an immediate rollback to previous stable policy
c.rollbackScalepolicy('tenant-789', {force: true})
  .then(r => console.log('rollback started', r))
  .catch(e => console.error(e));
```

marco: CLI command for copy-paste: `redwoodctl dedicated rollback --tenant tenant-789 --policy-id last-stable`

nina: For migration note: older docs referenced `rollback_window_ms`. New name is `rollback_window_seconds`. Convert by dividing ms by 1000. Also mention that the rollback API now returns a `rollback_id` for tracking.

jess: I'll add a tiny example of how to query status with rollback_id using the API: `GET /v2/dedicated/rollbacks/{rollback_id}` (docs link).

docs-bot: preview for PR #2491 ready: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/pr-2491 (lint passed)

marco: LGTM, small nit: change "two cooldown windows" -> "up to two cooldown windows (2 x cooldown_seconds)" to be explicit.

jess: Good call. I'll update phrasing and push. Thanks! :rocket:
